questions.question_text: Chemical composition of asbestos:
questions.explanation: Asbestos is a group of naturally occurring silicate minerals composed of thin, fibrous crystals known chemically as aluminosilicates.

questions.question_text: Which among the following is classified as folate antagonist:
questions.explanation: Methotrexate is a well-known antimetabolite and antifolate drug used in cancer chemotherapy and autoimmune diseases.

questions.question_text: Gynaecomastia may be the possible side effects of one of the following drug:
questions.explanation: Ketoconazole inhibits steroidogenesis, including testosterone synthesis, which can lead to gynecomastia as a side effect.

questions.question_text: When at least $51\%$ shares of business organisation are in the hands of government it is called:
questions.explanation: A government company is defined as any company in which not less than $51\%$ of the paid-up share capital is held by the government.

questions.question_text: Myristicin is a chemical constituent of:
questions.explanation: Myristicin is a naturally occurring organic compound found in nutmeg essential oil.

questions.question_text: A cationic surfactant is:
questions.explanation: Cetrimide is a cationic surfactant commonly used as an antiseptic and disinfectant.

questions.question_text: Which type of mill is used for grinding sulphonamide drug?
questions.explanation: Fluid energy mills (jet mills) are used for ultra-fine grinding of heat-sensitive substances like certain sulfonamides.

questions.question_text: Mail order business is:
questions.explanation: Mail order business is a form of retailing where goods are sold through the mail or postal service.

questions.question_text: Which drug is used for the detection of boric acid?
questions.explanation: Turmeric paper contains curcumin, which reacts with boric acid to form a reddish-brown complex (rosocyanin), used in detection.

questions.question_text: A strong dog poison is:
questions.explanation: Strychnine is an extremely toxic alkaloid traditionally used as a pesticide, notably against vertebrates such as stray dogs.

questions.question_text: The ability of the firm to meet its current liability is measured by:
questions.explanation: Liquidity ratios measure a company's ability to pay off its short-term debts and current liabilities.

questions.question_text: Drugs which increases respiratory tract fluid is called:
questions.explanation: Expectorants are pharmacological agents that increase bronchial secretion and respiratory tract fluid.

questions.question_text: Precursor glycoside of digitoxin:
questions.explanation: Purpurea glycoside A is the primary biosynthetic precursor to digitoxin found in Digitalis purpurea.

questions.question_text: Storage condition for dried plasma:
questions.explanation: Dried human plasma is typically stored at temperatures not exceeding $25^{\circ}\text{C}$ to maintain stability.

questions.question_text: Aloe contain barbaloin which is a:
questions.explanation: Barbaloin (aloin) is an anthraquinone derivative containing a C-glycosidic bond.

questions.question_text: An example of cholinomimetic alkaloid is:
questions.explanation: Pilocarpine is a naturally occurring plant alkaloid that acts as a direct-acting cholinomimetic.

questions.question_text: Beta blocker with membrane stabilizing activity:
questions.explanation: Propranolol possesses intrinsic local anesthetic or membrane-stabilizing activity among beta-blockers.

questions.question_text: A journal is a book of:
questions.explanation: A journal is known as a book of original entry where financial transactions are first recorded.

questions.question_text: A resin of animal origin:
questions.explanation: Shellac is a natural resin secreted by the female lac insect.

questions.question_text: All the particles passes through a sieve No. 44 and not more than $40\%$ through a sieve No. 85 called as:
questions.explanation: Moderately fine powder standards require all particles to pass through sieve No. 44 and not more than $40\%$ through sieve No. 85.

questions.question_text: Vein Islet number of Digitalis Purpurea:
questions.explanation: The vein islet number for Digitalis purpurea typically ranges from 15 to 26.

questions.question_text: Plant constituent used in the preparation of mosquito coils:
questions.explanation: Pyrethrins extracted from Pyrethrum flowers are widely used as natural insecticides in mosquito coils.

questions.question_text: Richest source of Lecithin:
questions.explanation: Egg yolk and soybeans are well-known rich natural sources of lecithin (phosphatidylcholine).

questions.question_text: Mevalonic acid formation is catalysed by the enzyme:
questions.explanation: HMG-CoA reductase catalyzes the rate-limiting step in cholesterol biosynthesis, reducing HMG-CoA to mevalonate.

questions.question_text: Enzyme referred as spreading factor:
questions.explanation: Hyaluronidase is known as the spreading factor because it degrades hyaluronic acid, increasing tissue permeability.

questions.question_text: The ex-officio member of Pharmacy Council of India is:
questions.explanation: The Director of the Central Drugs Laboratory (CDL) serves as an ex-officio member of the Pharmacy Council of India.

questions.question_text: Casein is an example of:
questions.explanation: Casein is a major phosphoprotein found in mammalian milk.

questions.question_text: Immunoglobulin found on lymphocyte surface of new born:
questions.explanation: IgM and IgD are typically expressed on the surface of mature B lymphocytes.

questions.question_text: Antigenic preparations made from extra cellular toxins:
questions.explanation: Toxoids are modified bacterial exotoxins that have been detoxified while retaining their antigenicity.

questions.question_text: Enzyme which is used in the treatment of leukaemia:
questions.explanation: L-asparaginase is utilized in chemotherapy to treat acute lymphoblastic leukemia by depleting circulating asparagine.

questions.question_text: One tea spoon full is:
questions.explanation: Traditionally, a standard metric teaspoonful in pharmacy corresponds to approximately $4\text{ ml}$ or $5\text{ ml}$ ($4\text{ ml}$ is common in classic British/Indian pharmacopoeial equivalence tables).

questions.question_text: A drug consist, in full or in whole or in part, of any filthy, putrid or decomposed substance:
questions.explanation: Under drug regulations, a drug containing filthy, putrid, or decomposed substances is legally classified as adulterated.

questions.question_text: Standards of disinfectant fluid comes under:
questions.explanation: Schedule O of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act outlines standards for disinfectant fluids.

questions.question_text: Which vitamin is known as antisterility factor?
questions.explanation: Vitamin E is historically known as the anti-sterility factor because deficiency was found to cause reproductive failure in rats.

questions.question_text: Sodium chloride injection IP contains:
questions.explanation: Normal saline (Sodium Chloride Injection IP) is an isotonic solution containing $0.9\%\text{ w/v}$ of sodium chloride.

questions.question_text: An opaque covering agent used in bleaches:
questions.explanation: Titanium dioxide is a widely used opacifying agent in cosmetic and pharmaceutical formulations.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following dryer is known as Lyophiliser?
questions.explanation: A freeze dryer is also known as a lyophiliser, which removes water by sublimation under vacuum.

questions.question_text: Autoclaving of ampoules in a dye bath as:
questions.explanation: The dye bath test involving autoclaving is a standard method for leaker testing of sealed ampoules.

questions.question_text: High count of WBC's is an indication of:
questions.explanation: Leukemia is characterized by a significant, uncontrolled increase in the count of white blood cells (WBCs).

questions.question_text: Example of an antioxidant:
questions.explanation: Gallic acid and its derivatives are well-known phenolic antioxidants.

questions.question_text: Isotonic vehicle used to prepare ophthalmic solution:
questions.explanation: $1.9\%$ Boric acid solution is isotonic with tear fluid and serves as an ophthalmic vehicle and buffer.

questions.question_text: Repeated administration of drug results in cell receptor blockage. This is known as:
questions.explanation: Tolerance describes the gradual decrease in responsiveness to a drug following repeated administration.

questions.question_text: Sterilization by autoclaving:
questions.explanation: Autoclaving uses steam under pressure, which is classified as moist heat sterilization.

questions.question_text: Keller-Killiani test is the identification test for:
questions.explanation: Keller-Killiani test is used to detect deoxysugars characteristic of cardiac glycosides present in Digitalis.

questions.question_text: THC is a constituent found in the plant:
questions.explanation: Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) is the principal psychoactive constituent of the Cannabis plant.

questions.question_text: Which is the highly perfused organ in the body?
questions.explanation: The liver receives dual blood supply and is among the most highly perfused organs in the human body.

questions.question_text: Diatomaceous earth is the other name of:
questions.explanation: Diatomaceous earth is also known as kieselguhr and is used as a filtering aid.

questions.question_text: Cotton consists of epidermal trichomes of species:
questions.explanation: Purified cotton consists of epidermal trichomes of seeds of Gossypium species such as Gossypium herbaceum.

questions.question_text: The working principle of hammer mill:
questions.explanation: A hammer mill primarily operates on the principle of impact to reduce particle size.

questions.question_text: Partial or complete removal of top or bottom of a tablet is known as:
questions.explanation: Capping is the partial or complete separation of the top or bottom crowns of a tablet from the main body.

questions.question_text: Mother clove is an adulterant of:
questions.explanation: Mother cloves (ripe fruits of the clove tree) are commonly used as an adulterant for genuine clove flower buds.

questions.question_text: Tablets are designed to exert local effect in throat:
questions.explanation: Lozenges are solid preparations designed to dissolve slowly in the mouth to release medication for a local effect in the throat.

questions.question_text: A plant drug which lowers blood pressure:
questions.explanation: Rauwolfia serpentina contains reserpine, a well-known alkaloid used as an antihypertensive agent.

questions.question_text: The minimum required area to open a retail drug store is:
questions.explanation: According to pharmacy regulations in many jurisdictions (such as India), the minimum area required for a retail drug store is 10 square meters.

questions.question_text: Enteric coated tablets are designed to release medicament in:
questions.explanation: Enteric coatings are acid-resistant and designed to prevent release in the stomach, releasing the drug in the alkaline environment of the small intestine.

questions.question_text: Dryer used for the production of milk powder:
questions.explanation: Spray drying is the standard industrial method used for producing milk powder from liquid milk due to rapid evaporation.

questions.question_text: Vapaside is an insecticide which is formulated from:
questions.explanation: Pyrethrum is widely used as a natural botanical insecticide.

questions.question_text: Jesuit's bark is the synonym of:
questions.explanation: Cinchona bark is historically known as Jesuit's bark because it was introduced to Europe by Jesuit missionaries.

questions.question_text: Renin a proteolytic enzyme which is produced in:
questions.explanation: Renin is an aspartic protease synthesized, stored, and secreted by the juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney.

questions.question_text: An example of potassium sparing diuretics:
questions.explanation: Triamterene is a potassium-sparing diuretic that acts directly on the renal distal tubules.

questions.question_text: Alkylating agent used as antineoplastic drug:
questions.explanation: Nitrogen mustard is a classic alkylating antineoplastic agent.

questions.question_text: Abrasive agent used in dentifrices:
questions.explanation: Calcium carbonate is commonly used as a polishing and abrasive agent in toothpaste formulations.

questions.question_text: First line agent used in Tuberculosis:
questions.explanation: Isoniazid is a primary first-line medication for the treatment of tuberculosis.

questions.question_text: Reagent used for the identification of cellulose:
questions.explanation: Chlorzinc iodine (sometimes referred to as van Urk's or similar specific identification reagents) or specialized iodine tests are used, but among choices, Vanurk's or equivalent is selected; typically chlorzinc iodine turns cellulose blue/violet.

questions.question_text: Drug used in uterine inertia:
questions.explanation: Oxytocin is used to stimulate uterine contractions in uterine inertia during labor.

questions.question_text: Dimethicone is the other name of:
questions.explanation: Dimethicone is polymerized siloxane, commonly known as medical grade silicone oil.

questions.question_text: Drug used in ulcerative colitis:
questions.explanation: Sulfasalazine is a standard anti-inflammatory drug used in the management of ulcerative colitis.

questions.question_text: Drug that act by lowering the plasma LDL level:
questions.explanation: Fibrates like clofibrate are lipid-lowering agents that reduce plasma triglyceride and LDL levels.

questions.question_text: Other name of regenerated cellulose:
questions.explanation: Rayon is a manufactured fiber composed of regenerated cellulose.

questions.question_text: An example of rapidly acting anticoagulant:
questions.explanation: Heparin acts rapidly as an injectable anticoagulant, unlike oral anticoagulants such as warfarin.

questions.question_text: Water soluble constituent of Ergot:
questions.explanation: Ergometrine (ergonovine) is uniquely water-soluble among the principal ergot alkaloids.

questions.question_text: Yeast is the richest source of:
questions.explanation: Yeast is well-known as an exceptionally rich natural source of B-complex vitamins.

questions.question_text: Drug used to test gastric acid secretion:
questions.explanation: Histamine (or pentagastrin) is historically used as a stimulant to test gastric acid secretory capacity.

questions.question_text: Shick test is performed to test the degree of immunity against:
questions.explanation: The Schick test is a clinical skin test used to determine whether a person is susceptible to diphtheria.

questions.question_text: Example of ultra short acting barbiturates:
questions.explanation: Thiopental sodium is an ultra-short-acting barbiturate used for induction of anesthesia.

questions.question_text: Rasping method is used to prepare:
questions.explanation: Lemon oil and other citrus oils are traditionally obtained by the rasping (or ecuelle) method from the fruit peel.

questions.question_text: Chemical name of plaster of paris:
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulfate hemihydrate ($CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O$).

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a beta-lactamase inhibitor?
questions.explanation: Sulbactam is a beta-lactamase inhibitor given in combination with beta-lactam antibiotics.

questions.question_text: Oxytocin is the hormone released from:
questions.explanation: Oxytocin is synthesized in the hypothalamus and released from the posterior lobe of the pituitary gland.

questions.question_text: Scurvy is the deficiency symptom of vitamin:
questions.explanation: Scurvy is caused by a deficiency of vitamin C (ascorbic acid).
